name: Elioenai
overview: Elioenai is a male biblical figure mentioned as a descendant of Zattu. He is uniquely noted for being among those who had married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:27. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Elioenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional aspect toward the Lord. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 10:27 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Elioenai as a descendant of Zattu, establishing a clear familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded, and no surname or tribal connections are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Elioenai’s significance lies in his inclusion among those who had married foreign wives, an issue addressed during the post-exilic reforms recorded in Ezra. His mention highlights the challenges faced by the returning Israelites in maintaining covenantal purity. As a descendant of Zattu, Elioenai represents a lineage involved in the restoration efforts under divine guidance.
